newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Overnight rain helps Brazil soybean regions-coops.
newsitem.headline: Overnight rain helps Brazil soybean regions-coops.

text.p: A cold front brought much-needed rain to Brazil's key soybean growing region of Rio Grande do Sul overnight, temporarily alleviating the dryness which has affected some areas of the state, growers said.

"It rained last night," said a technician at Emater, the state's technical assistance and development organization. "We don't know yet if the entire state benefited but it looks like the rains will continue."
The expert said the state's soybean crop was developing normally, with 94 percent in the vegetative growth stage and the remaining six percent in the flowering phase.
"This is more or less within the historical average," he said. "There is no problem at all."
Temperatures had dropped after the rains from a maximum of 37 degrees Celsius in Porto Alegre on Wednesday to between 30 and 32 degrees on Thursday.
In the other main growing region of Parana, it also rained overnight.
"We got around 13 mm of rain," said Ernani Campanati of the Coopavel cooperative in Cascavel. He predicted summer weather would continue with high temperatures and occasional showers.
